authorization: User explicitly authorized 6 BRANCHING AB-R cycles conforming to NEXT_6_PROPOSAL.md
adaptive_context: MATE10 and BRANCH8 outputs explicitly exploratory, no untouched confirmatory holdout
aim: Test opportunities as sufficient sorting mechanism versus effects of sequential filtering without explicit similarity preferences

assumptions.sex: binary 50/50, exclusively heterosexual synthetic; no empirical claim
assumptions.preferences: women 0.6 status+0.4 looks; men 0.4 status+0.6 looks, plus fixed dyadic noise for N09
assumptions.outcomes: Pearson r of initial desirability among matched, % population matched including singles, median absolute gap; utility-based graph blocking pairs when defined
assumptions.stats: descriptive across 5 seeds with per-seed CSV; no external replication, no p-value based on agents as iid humans

cycles.A: Compare DA and online sequential filtering on exactly same ex ante regular bipartite opportunity graph
cycles.B: H_static DA sorting from preference and mutual feasibility; H_dynamic online thresholds add sorting over static greedy after opportunity matching; H_null differences explained by information timing
cycles.C: N400 200 men/women, k=20 and k=60 regular exposure graphs; 5 seeds, same fixed per-edge utility with Gaussian dyadic error sd=.08; three algorithms DA (full graph ranking; outside .05), greedy early accept (utility >=.05), adaptive sequential (q0=.8, qmin=.05, fatigue .015 per observed failure + .01 only for unilateral accept). Graph edges processed in same pre-drawn random schedule for sequential variants; DA sees all edges, explicitly informational advantage. Endpoints r,coverage,matched-mean utility,blocking edge count; invariants unique pairs, DA no blocking pairs, all matches on graph.
cycles.D: Paridad del conjunto de parejas potenciales, no de tiempo/información; contrast greedy vs dynamic strongest timing control. N total 400.

cycles.A: Repair low-power N03 via balanced local pools, controlled distinct exposures
cycles.B: H0 observed local effects vanish with balanced composition and sufficient successful matches; H1 residual pool-size sorting remains
cycles.C: N1200 balanced sexes, pool sizes 100,300,1200, exactly T40 distinct scheduled encounters/personal until match (each pool has >=50 opposite); same q0=.82 fatigue=.015 rejection=.005; five seeds and same population per seed, randomized pool assignments. Pilot rule from prereg: 2 independent seeds to assess if min coverage >=40% and >=50 pairs per condition; otherwise stop without tuning parameters. Proceed with all five only if gate met. Record distribution of pairs/pool and effective exposures.
cycles.D: Identical potential exposures per agent pre-match, opportunities cease upon matching; pool compositions differ otherwise. Record denominator and power caveats.

cycles.A: Asynchrony under exactly same bipartite edge graph and 40 planned evaluations per person
cycles.B: H0 ordering/exposure asymmetry changes outcomes only via realised exposure; H1 fixed reciprocal opportunity graph but timing generates differences
cycles.C: N400, 200/sex, k40 random regular bipartite graph, T40. Same score and pair-specific dyadic error sd=.06, q0=.8 fatigue=.015 by own unsuccessful views, no feedback after unilateral rejection (in async unresolved until second side view). Three variants: sync both view same edge at same round; async men evaluate edges in order, women a fixed shuffled offset order, likes persist; async with likes expiring after 5 ticks. 5 seeds with paired conditions and exact same prospective edges. Compare exposure-realisation, r,coverage, gap, distinct/mutually evaluated edges. Fix irrevocable left, exit on match. Ensure no duplicate matches.
cycles.D: Equal planned exposure graph, not equal realised degree among agents because exits endogenous; expiration changes feasible pair sets.
